Key.Original: Alignment: Allies%1Capital: Warsaw%1National Language: Polish%1Demonyms: Polish, Pole%1%1During the Second World War, the Polish Resistance emerged as a vast underground movement opposing German occupation. Composed of civilians and former soldiers, it carried out sabotage, intelligence gathering and armed uprisings, including the Warsaw Uprising of 1944. Operating in secrecy under brutal conditions, the resistance became a symbol of national defiance and played a crucial role in preserving Poland’s military and cultural identity during the war.%1
